1	# Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks: Time Horizon Doubling Every 7 Months
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	- URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14499
     5	- Authors: Thomas Kwa, Ben West, Joel Becker, et al. — Model Evaluation & Threat Research (METR)
     6	- Published: March 2025
     7	
     8	## The Time Horizon Metric
     9	
    10	The paper proposes a new metric for quantifying AI autonomous capabilities: the **50% task-completion time horizon** — the duration of tasks (measured by how long they take skilled human professionals) that an AI model can complete with 50% success rate. This provides an intuitive, human-grounded measure of real-world AI capability that allows comparison across vastly different models (e.g., GPT-2 vs. Claude 3.7 Sonnet).
    11	
    12	The methodology involves three steps: (1) assembling a diverse suite of 170 software/research tasks, (2) timing skilled humans and measuring AI agent success rates on these tasks, and (3) fitting a logistic model to estimate the task duration at which each AI agent achieves 50% success.
    13	
    14	![Methodology overview](./assets/figure_2.jpg)
    15	
    16	## Task Suite: 170 Tasks from 1 Second to 8 Hours
    17	
    18	The benchmark combines three task suites: HCAST (97 diverse software tasks, 1 min–30 hrs), RE-Bench (7 difficult ML research engineering tasks, all 8 hrs), and Software Atomic Actions / SWAA (66 short single-step tasks, 1 sec–30 sec). Over 800 human baselines totaling 2,529 hours were collected.
    19	
    20	| Family | Human Time | Description |
    21	|---|---|---|
    22	| find_shell_script | 3 seconds | Multiple choice: "Which file is a shell script?" |
    23	| wikipedia_research | 1 minute | Research simple factual information from Wikipedia |
    24	| oxdna_simple | 9 minutes | Detect and fix a bug in molecular dynamics simulation input files |
    25	| munge_data | 56 minutes | Write a Python script to transform JSON data by inferring conversion rules |
    26	| cuda_backtesting | 8 hours | Implement custom CUDA kernels for 30x speedup of a backtesting tool |
    27	
    28	## Exponential Growth in AI Time Horizon (2019–2025)
    29	
    30	The central finding is that the 50% time horizon has grown exponentially from 2019 to 2025, with a **doubling time of approximately 207 days (~7 months)** and an R² of 0.97. Key data points across models:
    31	
    32	| Model | Release Period | 50% Time Horizon |
    33	|---|---|---|
    34	| GPT-2 | 2019 | ~2 seconds |
    35	| GPT-3 (davinci-002) | 2020 | ~9 seconds |
    36	| GPT-3.5-turbo-instruct | 2023 | ~36 seconds |
    37	| GPT-4 (0314) | 2023 | ~5 minutes |
    38	| GPT-4o | 2024 | ~9 minutes |
    39	| Claude 3 Opus | 2024 | ~6 minutes |
    40	| Claude 3.5 Sonnet (New) | 2024 | ~28 minutes |
    41	| o1 | 2024 | ~39 minutes |
    42	| Claude 3.7 Sonnet | 2025 | ~54 minutes |
    43	| o3 | 2025 | ~1 hour 50 minutes |
    44	
    45	![Exponential trend in AI time horizon](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
    46	
    47	The 2023–2025 growth rate is approximately 20% faster than the overall 2019–2025 rate, suggesting possible acceleration. The 80% time horizon (tasks completed 80% of the time) shows a similar trend but with horizons roughly 5x shorter.
    48	
    49	![Per-model success probability curves](./assets/figure_3.jpg)
    50	
    51	## Drivers and Limitations
    52	
    53	Progress appears driven by: **improved logical reasoning**, **better tool use**, **greater reliability and self-awareness** in task execution, and **ability to adapt to mistakes**. However, performance is notably lower on less structured, "messier" tasks. External validity remains an open question — the tasks do not perfectly represent the average segment of real-world intellectual labor, though supplementary experiments found little evidence that trends are slower on more realistic tasks.
    54	
    55	## Key Findings
    56	
    57	- **50% time horizon** provides a robust, intuitive metric for tracking AI autonomous capability growth, with R² = 0.97 over 6 years of model releases.
    58	- Frontier AI agents (o3) can now autonomously complete tasks that take skilled humans **nearly 2 hours**, up from 2 seconds for GPT-2 in 2019.
    59	- The doubling time is **~7 months**, with possible acceleration since 2024.
    60	- Naive extrapolation predicts AI will reach a **1-month time horizon (167 work hours) between mid-2028 and mid-2031**, implying automation of many month-long software projects.
    61	- Key capability drivers are reasoning, tool use, and error recovery; key limitations include poor performance on unstructured tasks and uncertain external validity to real-world job distributions.

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt, Emu
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.oxml.ns import nsmap
from pptx.oxml import parse_xml
import os

# Constants
SLIDE_WIDTH = Inches(13.333)
SLIDE_HEIGHT = Inches(7.5)
ASSETS_DIR = "/app/benchmark/assets"
OUTPUT_PATH = "/app/output/final_deck.pptx"

# Color palette (dark, technical, data-forward)
BG_COLOR = RGBColor(0x0F, 0x11, 0x17)  # near-black
ACCENT_COLOR = RGBColor(0x3A, 0x9B, 0xD6)  # steel blue
TEXT_COLOR = RGBColor(0xE8, 0xE8, 0xEC)  # off-white
MUTED_COLOR = RGBColor(0x8A, 0x8F, 0x98)  # grey
HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = RGBColor(0xFF, 0x6B, 0x35)  # orange highlight


def set_slide_bg(slide, color):
    background = slide.background
    fill = background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color


def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=18, bold=False, color=TEXT_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Calibri"):
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.color.rgb = color
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = align
    return tf


def add_bullet_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, bullets, font_size=16, color=TEXT_COLOR, bullet_color=ACCENT_COLOR, font_name="Calibri"):
    tf = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height).text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, bullet in enumerate(bullets):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = bullet
        p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
        p.font.color.rgb = color
        p.font.name = font_name
        p.level = 0
        p.space_after = Pt(10)
    return tf


def add_table(slide, left, top, width, rows, cols, data, font_size=14, header_color=ACCENT_COLOR, bg_color=RGBColor(0x1A, 0x1D, 0x26), text_color=TEXT_COLOR):
    table = slide.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, left, top, width, Inches(0.6 * rows)).table
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            cell = table.cell(r, c)
            cell.text = data[r][c]
            cell.text_frame.word_wrap = True
            for p in cell.text_frame.paragraphs:
                p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
                p.font.color.rgb = text_color
                p.font.name = "Calibri"
                if r == 0:
                    p.font.bold = True
                    p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
            if r == 0:
                cell.fill.solid()
                cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = header_color
            else:
                cell.fill.solid()
                cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = bg_color if r % 2 == 0 else RGBColor(0x13, 0x15, 0x1C)
    return table


def add_figure(slide, img_path, left, top, width, height):
    if os.path.exists(img_path):
        slide.shapes.add_picture(img_path, left, top, width, height)
    else:
        add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, f"[Image not found: {img_path}]", font_size=12, color=MUTED_COLOR)


# Create presentation
prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = SLIDE_WIDTH
prs.slide_height = SLIDE_HEIGHT

blank_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # blank

# ============================================================
# Slide 1: Title
# ============================================================
slide1 = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout)
set_slide_bg(slide1, BG_COLOR)

add_textbox(slide1, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.8), Inches(11.7), Inches(1.2),
            "Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks",
            font_size=40, bold=True, color=TEXT_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

add_textbox(slide1, Inches(0.8), Inches(3.0), Inches(11.7), Inches(0.6),
            "Time Horizon Doubling Every ~7 Months",
            font_size=28, bold=False, color=ACCENT_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

add_textbox(slide1, Inches(0.8), Inches(4.0), Inches(11.7), Inches(0.5),
            "Thomas Kwa, Ben West, Joel Becker, et al. — METR  |  arXiv:2503.14499  |  March 2025",
            font_size=16, bold=False, color=MUTED_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

add_textbox(slide1, Inches(0.8), Inches(5.0), Inches(11.7), Inches(1.0),
            "Headline Finding: The 50% task-completion time horizon for frontier AI agents has been doubling approximately every 207 days (~7 months) since 2019, reaching nearly 2 hours with o3.",
            font_size=18, bold=False, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# ============================================================
# Slide 2: Metric Explained
# ============================================================
slide2 = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout)
set_slide_bg(slide2, BG_COLOR)

add_textbox(slide2, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.4), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.8),
            "A New Metric: 50% Task-Completion Time Horizon",
            font_size=32, bold=True, color=TEXT_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

add_textbox(slide2, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.2), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.6),
            "A human-grounded, intuitive measure of autonomous AI capability that enables comparison across models from GPT-2 to o3.",
            font_size=16, bold=False, color=MUTED_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Three-step flow
steps = [
    ("1. Assemble Task Suite", "170 diverse software / research tasks ranging from 1 second to 8 hours of skilled human effort."),
    ("2. Collect Human Baselines & AI Rates", "Time skilled humans on each task; measure AI agent success rates under controlled conditions."),
    ("3. Fit Logistic Model", "Estimate the task duration at which the model achieves exactly 50% success — the time horizon."),
]

for i, (title, desc) in enumerate(steps):
    left = Inches(0.6 + i * 4.1)
    top = Inches(2.0)
    width = Inches(3.7)
    height = Inches(2.2)
    # card background
    shape = slide2.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(0x1A, 0x1D, 0x26)
    shape.line.color.rgb = ACCENT_COLOR
    shape.line.width = Pt(1.5)
    # title
    add_textbox(slide2, left + Inches(0.15), top + Inches(0.15), width - Inches(0.3), Inches(0.5),
                title, font_size=18, bold=True, color=ACCENT_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
    # desc
    add_textbox(slide2, left + Inches(0.15), top + Inches(0.7), width - Inches(0.3), Inches(1.3),
                desc, font_size=15, bold=False, color=TEXT_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Figure 2
add_textbox(slide2, Inches(0.6), Inches(4.5), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.4),
            "Methodology Overview (Figure 2)", font_size=16, bold=True, color=MUTED_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
add_figure(slide2, os.path.join(ASSETS_DIR, "figure_2.jpg"), Inches(0.6), Inches(4.9), Inches(12.0), Inches(2.2))

# ============================================================
# Slide 3: Task Suite Overview
# ============================================================
slide3 = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout)
set_slide_bg(slide3, BG_COLOR)

add_textbox(slide3, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.4), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.8),
            "170 Tasks Spanning 3 Seconds to 8 Hours of Human Effort",
            font_size=32, bold=True, color=TEXT_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

add_textbox(slide3, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.1), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.4),
            "Three complementary benchmarks with >800 human baselines (2,529 hours total).",
            font_size=16, bold=False, color=MUTED_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Suite table
suite_data = [
    ["Source", "Tasks", "Human Time Range", "Description"],
    ["HCAST", "97", "1 min – 30 hrs", "Diverse software engineering tasks (debugging, refactoring, data munging)."],
    ["RE-Bench", "7", "~8 hrs each", "Difficult ML research engineering tasks (e.g., custom CUDA kernel backtesting)."],
    ["SWAA", "66", "1 sec – 30 sec", "Short single-step atomic actions (e.g., identify shell scripts, quick lookups)."],
]
add_table(slide3, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.7), Inches(12.0), 4, 4, suite_data, font_size=15)

# Example tasks table
add_textbox(slide3, Inches(0.6), Inches(4.0), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.4),
            "Example Tasks by Human Duration", font_size=18, bold=True, color=ACCENT_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

example_data = [
    ["Task Family", "Human Time", "Description"],
    ["find_shell_script", "3 seconds", "Multiple choice: 'Which file is a shell script?'"],
    ["wikipedia_research", "1 minute", "Research simple factual information from Wikipedia."],
    ["oxdna_simple", "9 minutes", "Detect and fix a bug in molecular dynamics simulation input files."],
    ["munge_data", "56 minutes", "Write a Python script to transform JSON data by inferring conversion rules."],
    ["cuda_backtesting", "8 hours", "Implement custom CUDA kernels for 30× speedup of a backtesting tool."],
]
add_table(slide3, Inches(0.6), Inches(4.5), Inches(12.0), 6, 3, example_data, font_size=14)

# ============================================================
# Slide 4: Exponential Trend
# ============================================================
slide4 = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout)
set_slide_bg(slide4, BG_COLOR)

add_textbox(slide4, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.3), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.8),
            "AI Task Horizon Grew from 2 Seconds (GPT-2) to ~1 Hour 50 Minutes (o3) in 6 Years",
            font_size=30, bold=True, color=TEXT_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

add_figure(slide4, os.path.join(ASSETS_DIR, "figure_1.jpg"), Inches(0.6), Inches(1.1), Inches(12.0), Inches(5.4))

# Stats overlay
add_textbox(slide4, Inches(0.6), Inches(6.6), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.5),
            "Doubling time ≈ 207 days (~7 months)  |  R² = 0.97  |  2023–2025 growth ~20% faster than 2019–2025 baseline",
            font_size=16, bold=True, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# ============================================================
# Slide 5: Model-by-Model Success Curves
# ============================================================
slide5 = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout)
set_slide_bg(slide5, BG_COLOR)

add_textbox(slide5, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.3), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.8),
            "Success Probability Drops Sharply as Task Length Increases for All Models",
            font_size=30, bold=True, color=TEXT_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

add_textbox(slide5, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.9), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.4),
            "Frontier models push the curve rightward: Claude 3.7 Sonnet (~54 min) and o3 (~1h 50m) extend the tail far beyond GPT-2 (~2 sec).",
            font_size=16, bold=False, color=MUTED_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

add_figure(slide5, os.path.join(ASSETS_DIR, "figure_3.jpg"), Inches(0.6), Inches(1.4), Inches(12.0), Inches(5.4))

add_textbox(slide5, Inches(0.6), Inches(6.8), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.4),
            "The 80% time horizon follows a similar trajectory but remains roughly 5× shorter than the 50% horizon.",
            font_size=15, bold=False, color=MUTED_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# ============================================================
# Slide 6: Drivers of Progress
# ============================================================
slide6 = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout)
set_slide_bg(slide6, BG_COLOR)

add_textbox(slide6, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.4), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.8),
            "Reasoning, Tool Use, and Error Recovery Drive Time Horizon Growth",
            font_size=32, bold=True, color=TEXT_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Drivers
bullets = [
    "• Improved logical reasoning — models plan and decompose multi-step problems more effectively.",
    "• Better tool use — integration with IDEs, terminals, and APIs expands actionable scope.",
    "• Greater reliability and self-awareness — models recognize when they are stuck and backtrack.",
    "• Ability to adapt to mistakes — error recovery reduces cascading failure on long tasks.",
]
add_bullet_textbox(slide6, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.4), Inches(12.0), Inches(2.8), bullets, font_size=18)

# Limitations
add_textbox(slide6, Inches(0.6), Inches(4.4), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.5),
            "Key Limitations", font_size=22, bold=True, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

limit_bullets = [
    "• Performance is notably lower on less structured, 'messier' tasks that lack clear success criteria.",
    "• External validity remains open — benchmark tasks may not perfectly represent real-world intellectual labor distributions.",
    "• Supplementary experiments found little evidence that trends are slower on more realistic tasks, but generalization is not guaranteed.",
]
add_bullet_textbox(slide6, Inches(0.6), Inches(4.9), Inches(12.0), Inches(2.2), limit_bullets, font_size=17)

# ============================================================
# Slide 7: Extrapolation and Forecasts
# ============================================================
slide7 = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout)
set_slide_bg(slide7, BG_COLOR)

add_textbox(slide7, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.4), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.8),
            "Extrapolation Predicts Month-Long Task Automation by 2028–2031",
            font_size=32, bold=True, color=TEXT_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

add_textbox(slide7, Inches(0.6), Inches(1.2), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.5),
            "If the exponential trend continues, frontier AI would autonomously complete tasks requiring ~167 work hours (1 month) within the next 3–6 years.",
            font_size=18, bold=False, color=MUTED_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Timeline visual (text-based)
timeline_items = [
    ("2019", "GPT-2", "~2 seconds"),
    ("2023", "GPT-4", "~5 minutes"),
    ("2024", "o1 / Claude 3.5", "~28–39 minutes"),
    ("2025", "o3 / Claude 3.7", "~54 min – 1h 50m"),
    ("2028–2031", "Projected frontier", "~1 month (167 hrs)"),
]

for i, (year, model, horizon) in enumerate(timeline_items):
    left = Inches(0.6 + i * 2.45)
    top = Inches(2.2)
    width = Inches(2.2)
    height = Inches(2.4)
    shape = slide7.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(0x1A, 0x1D, 0x26)
    shape.line.color.rgb = ACCENT_COLOR if i < 4 else HIGHLIGHT_COLOR
    shape.line.width = Pt(2)
    add_textbox(slide7, left + Inches(0.1), top + Inches(0.1), width - Inches(0.2), Inches(0.4),
                year, font_size=16, bold=True, color=ACCENT_COLOR if i < 4 else HIGHLIGHT_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)
    add_textbox(slide7, left + Inches(0.1), top + Inches(0.55), width - Inches(0.2), Inches(0.5),
                model, font_size=14, bold=True, color=TEXT_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)
    add_textbox(slide7, left + Inches(0.1), top + Inches(1.1), width - Inches(0.2), Inches(0.8),
                horizon, font_size=13, bold=False, color=MUTED_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# Caveats
add_textbox(slide7, Inches(0.6), Inches(5.0), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.4),
            "Caveats", font_size=20, bold=True, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

caveat_bullets = [
    "• Extrapolation assumes no fundamental slowdown or saturation in scaling laws.",
    "• External validity: month-long benchmark tasks may still differ from messy, real-world software projects.",
    "• 2023–2025 growth rate is ~20% faster than the 2019–2025 average, suggesting possible acceleration — or a transient burst.",
]
add_bullet_textbox(slide7, Inches(0.6), Inches(5.4), Inches(12.0), Inches(1.8), caveat_bullets, font_size=16)

# ============================================================
# Slide 8: Implications and Takeaways
# ============================================================
slide8 = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout)
set_slide_bg(slide8, BG_COLOR)

add_textbox(slide8, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.4), Inches(12.0), Inches(0.8),
            "Takeaways: Exponential Autonomous Capability Growth Demands Proactive Safety Governance",
            font_size=30, bold=True, color=TEXT_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

takeaways = [
    "1. Robust metric — The 50% time horizon is intuitive, human-grounded, and tracks autonomy with R² = 0.97 over 6 years of model releases.",
    "2. Consistent doubling — The horizon doubles every ~7 months; post-2024 data hints at acceleration, warranting close monitoring.",
    "3. Current frontier — o3 achieves ~1 hour 50 minutes of human-equivalent autonomous work, up from 2 seconds for GPT-2 in 2019.",
    "4. External validity is an open question — tasks are structured; performance on unstructured, 'messy' real-world labor remains uncertain.",
    "5. Governance imperative — Month-long automation by 2028–2031 would transform software R&D and labor markets; safety protocols, eval regimes, and policy frameworks must keep pace with this exponential trajectory.",
]

for i, text in enumerate(takeaways):
    top = Inches(1.4 + i * 1.05)
    add_textbox(slide8, Inches(0.6), top, Inches(12.0), Inches(0.9), text, font_size=18, bold=False, color=TEXT_COLOR, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Save
prs.save(OUTPUT_PATH)
print(f"Saved presentation to {OUTPUT_PATH}")
